page.layout: One page of verse in one column, set as stanzas with indent at the start of each stanza. Running head centred at the top, page number at top left. Catchword "Et" at the lower right. Show-through from the facing page at the right edge, not transcribed.

p.i: Et quam sollicitis cura laboribus Exercere solet strenua prouidam: Et quæ fida virum, fida domum iuuat Dispensare sagax res sibi creditas.
Quid tali melius? quid pretiosius Quisquam prætulerit coniuge: quæ decus Gemmarum superat clarior, atque opes Immensas Arabum & diuitis Indiæ?
Huius nectareis fidit amoribus Vir, certo & placitam pectore diligit, Morosisq; procul suspicionibus Concordes thalamos nil metuens colit.
Quantis illa domum diuitijs replet Ignavæ fugiens tædia inertiæ? Non plures tumidis hostibus inclitæ Victis marte Duces exuuias ferunt.
Hæc dulci satagit quæ placeant viro Iussisque obsequitur legitimis lubens. Socors cuncta fugit noxia quæ putat Et quærit vigili commoda pectore.
Lanas usque domum, linaq; conuehit, Exercetq; colos, filaque diuidens Pannos docta manu texere conficit Telarumque parat sedula copiam.
Non quæ littus arat sæpius exterum

page.notes: Show-through from the facing page at the right edge is not transcribed. The stain at the lower left is not text. "Morosisq;" and "linaq;", "exercetq;" carry a raised 3 over the q in print, shown here as "q;". The word "Et" at the foot is the catchword for the next page.
